title: Ancient Plague Evidence Found at Nicaea Fills Anatolian Gap in Pandemic History
description: Ancient plague evidence in Anatolia has been confirmed for the first time at the Iznik Roman Theater necropolis in Bursa, where skeletal remains of nearly 20 people yielded markers for the oldest known case of plague in the region, filling a key gap in the physical record of how the Justinianic Plague spread from Egypt toward Europe in the 6th century.

title: Scientists resurrect ancient proteins, offering new antibiotic leads
description: University of Oregon biologists have resurrected prehistoric proteins up to 160 million years old that carry natural antimicrobial properties. The revived molecules could inspire the design of new treatments for antibiotic-resistant infections, a pressing global health issue.
